Certified type:
- Category: Automatic instrument for weighing road vehicles in motion → I'd say "Weighing instrument" or "Automatic instrument for weighing road vehicles in motion". Given the categories suggested: "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system", "Fuel dispenser", "Taximeter", "Gas meter"... This is an automatic weighing instrument (axle load weighing). R134 is "Automatic instruments for weighing road vehicles in motion". Category could be "Automatic road vehicle weighing instrument". I'll use "Automatic instrument for weighing road vehicles in motion" as category, or maybe "Weighing instrument (WIM)". Let me use "Automatic instrument for weighing road vehicles in motion".
- Type designations: ["LL2/AW"]

Recommendation: R134, edition 2003. Accuracy classes: 1, 2 (from the table: Accuracy class 1, 2).

Test report: "the associated test reports from DELTA, DK, no. DANAK-199782, that includes 10 pages and 2 annexes (55 pages and 9 pages)". Role: type_evaluation_report. Pages: could be 10 pages plus annexes 55 and 9. I'll record pages: 10, and mention annexes in... The schema has id, date, pages, role. I'll set pages: 10 (main) — but maybe describe annexes? The schema only allows those fields. I could put pages as 10 and omit annex info, or represent total. Hmm. I'll put pages: 10 and maybe a note isn't allowed. Actually test_reports[]: id, date, pages, role. No free text. I'll just put id: "DANAK-199782", pages: 10. Or maybe represent total pages 74? The main report is 10 pages with 2 annexes (55 and 9 pages). I'll keep pages: 10. Hmm, but perhaps better to capture full extent. The schema is strict; I'll use 10.

Revision history: not present.

Characteristics table — this is a table with two accuracy classes (class 1 and class 2), so attributes vary by accuracy class. This is a configuration axis? Actually accuracy class is a configuration axis of the certified type. The table:

- Accuracy class: 1, 2
- Maximum capacity Max: 30 000 kg (both classes)
- Minimum capacity Min: ≥ 50×d (class 1), ≥ 10×d (class 2)
- Scale interval D: ≥ 10 kg (class 1), 50 kg (class 2)
- Maximum operation speed vmax: 3 km/h (class 1), 5 km/h (class 2)
- Minimum operation speed vmin: 1 km/h (both)
- Maximum transit speed: 30 km/h (both)
- Maximum number of axles: ≤ 12 (both)
- Direction of travel: dual (both)
- Scale interval for stationary load E: ≥ 0.8 μV (both) — note: that's odd, scale interval in μV? Actually "Scale interval for stationary load E ≥ 0.8 μV" — this appears to be a signal threshold. Anyway, record as given: value ≥ 0.8, unit μV.
- Power supply voltage: 12 V DC → value 12, unit "V", power_supply_type DC.
- Connected load cells: Shall comply with R60 → a string value.
- Temperature range for indicator: -10 °C / +40 °C → {min: -10, max: 40}, unit °C.

Since class 1 vs class 2 vary, use config_level with axis "accuracy_class". Per rule 5: config_level with axis. Values: {condition, value, unit_symbol}.

Note: rule 2 says every characteristic value MUST be an object with value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers. But config_level example in rule 5 shows {condition, value, unit_symbol}. Let me follow the schema: config_level[]: attribute, axis, values[]: {condition, value}. Rule 5 says values follow same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. I'll include unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers where appropriate.

Also model_family: only if cert covers >1 model variant. Here the type LL2/AW is a single model; the variation is by accuracy class, which is a configuration axis, not models. So no model_family.

Type-level characteristics (same for both classes):
- maximum_capacity: 30000 kg
- minimum_operation_speed: 1 km/h
- maximum_transit_speed: 30 km/h
- maximum_number_of_axles: {min: null, max: 12}
- direction_of_travel: "dual"
- scale_interval_stationary_load: {min: 0.8, max: null}, unit "μV" — value is "≥ 0.8 μV" → {min: 0.8, max: null}, unit_symbol "μV". Hmm, μV is microvolts — this seems like the signal per d for stationary load. Fine.
- power_supply_voltage: 12 V
- power_supply_type: "DC"
- connected_load_cells: "Shall comply with R60" — string value.
- indicator_temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 40}, unit °C.

Class-dependent (config_level, axis "accuracy_class"):
- minimum_capacity: class 1: "≥ 50×d" → formula string "50×d" with min... It's expressed as multiple of d. Value: {min: "50×d", max: null}? Or value as string "≥ 50×d". Rule: formulas/symbols keep as string. Since it's a multiple of scale interval d, I'd record value: "50×d" and maybe a note. Let me do value: {min: "50×d", max: null}? Hmm, that's mixing. Perhaps simpler: value: "≥ 50×d"? But rule says pure formulas kept as string; ranges become {min,max} with numbers. Since the bound is a formula, I think {min: "50×d", max: null} is acceptable but awkward. Alternatively value: "50×d" with attribute minimum_capacity_multiple_of_d. I'll do value: {min: "50×d", max: null}. Actually let me reconsider — the schema examples: `{min: 1000, max: null}` for ≥1000. Here it's ≥50d. I'll use {min: "50×d", max: null}. Hmm, but strict typing says min could be number | {min,max} | string. {min,max} values could be strings too. I'll go with {min: "50×d", max: null}.

Actually, maybe cleaner to name attribute "minimum_capacity" and value as string "50×d"? The ≥ indicates min. I'll keep {min: "50×d", max: null}.

- scale_interval_d: class 1: "≥ 10 kg" → {min: 10, max: null}, unit "kg". Class 2: 50 kg → 50, unit "kg".
- maximum_operation_speed_vmax: class 1: 3 km/h; class 2: 5 km/h.

The rule says matrix_tables for multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere. This fits config_level, so I'll skip matrix_tables. Actually, maybe include it anyway for preservation? I'll skip to keep clean. Hmm — "preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere". It fits config_level. Skip.

Components: none named (load cells are generic "shall comply with R60"). Could add a component with role "load cells" but type not named. I'll skip components.
